clue.text: Runs from disagreement? That's a lie

indicators.note: the runs are taken away from the word for disagreement

parts.note: friction is disagreement or clashing between people
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone accused of fleeing an argument dismisses the charge as untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs from' looks like fleeing, but 'from' is the deletion signal: R comes out of FRICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiction is invented story, so a falsehood can be called fiction.

clue.text: Rebellious figure completely hidden in fen with a northern set

indicators.note: the word for completely is placed inside fen

parts.note: taken as written
all means completely, wholly
to gel is to set, as jelly does

explanation.surface: A rebel is found lying in wait in the marshes with a group from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucifer, the fallen angel, rebelled against God and was cast out of heaven.

clue.text: Chartered Accountant to change when interrupted by 50 horsemen

indicators.note: the change word is broken into by the numeral

parts.note: to vary is to change
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An accountant changes career when fifty riders interrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavalry are soldiers who fight on horseback.

clue.text: Annoyed pub worker receiving rude comment

indicators.note: the pub-and-worker pair takes the comment inside it

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a dig is a snide remark
the ant is the crossword's standard worker insect

explanation.surface: A barman gets cross after a customer's insult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pub worker' reads as a barman, but it is two pieces joined, and 'receiving' takes the comment into their join.
explanation.definitionFit: Indignant means angered by something felt to be unjust.

clue.text: Knight showing reserve about the Spanish? Exactly

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight

indicators.note: the reserve word goes round the Spanish article

parts.note: icy describes a cold, reserved manner
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A knight is aloof towards the Spaniard, precisely so.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicely can mean precisely or just right, as in fits nicely.

clue.text: Task mostly incorporating second check for fingerprints?

indicators.note: the shortened task word takes the second's letter into its middle
most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a duty is a task one must do

explanation.surface: A detective's chore involves a follow-up inspection for prints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts DUTY to DUT, and 'incorporating' puts S inside it. The question mark marks the definition as one example of dusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Police dust surfaces with powder to reveal fingerprints, a typical forensic check.

clue.text: One investing in Deutschmark? Not bright

indicators.note: putting money in, so the numeral goes inside the currency letters

parts.note: DM is the abbreviation for the old German currency
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A foolish investor puts money into the German mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim means unintelligent, or literally lacking light.

clue.text: Small, unyielding splinter

parts.note: hard means firm, not giving way

explanation.surface: A tiny, tough sliver of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A shard is a sharp broken fragment of glass or pottery.

clue.text: Angry figures in Ancient Rome

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
IV, I and D are further Roman numerals: four, one and five hundred

explanation.surface: Someone was furious about the numbers of old Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole answer is a run of Roman numerals: L, IV, I, D (50, 4, 1, 500).
explanation.definitionFit: Livid is a common British word for extremely cross, furious.

clue.text: Navigational aid in competition given to a ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A navigation device is offered as a prize in a contest to a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass shows magnetic north and is used to find direction at sea.

clue.text: Collection of planets: Mars and — yes — lots spinning

indicators.note: whirling round, so the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: An astronomer enthuses that Mars and many other bodies are rotating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the pieces; the letters of MARS, YES and LOTS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Our system of the Sun and its orbiting bodies includes the eight planets.

clue.text: Fish responsible for some receding ripple effects

indicators.note: going backwards, so the found letters are read in reverse
only some of the letters of the following words are used

explanation.surface: A fish is blamed for the dying ripples on a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks LEE out of rippLE EFfects and 'receding' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The eel is a long, snake-like fish.

clue.text: Aim to go round edges of land and sea to get top prize

indicators.note: the aim word goes round, enclosing, the other pieces

parts.note: a goal is an aim

indicators.note: only the outer letters of land are used

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: Someone aims to sail round the coasts and seas in order to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edges of' takes the first and last letters of land; 'to go round' puts them and the sea inside the aim word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold is awarded for first place, the highest award in sporting events.

clue.text: Very dangerous rumours spread about rising newsman

indicators.note: the scrambled rumours letters go round the reversed piece
rumours spread are scattered, so their letters are rearranged
in a down clue rising means read from the bottom up, backwards

parts.note: ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: Gossip spreads about a journalist climbing the career ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' makes MURROUS of rumours; in a down answer 'rising' reverses the newsman, and 'about' wraps the anagram round him.
explanation.definitionFit: Murderous behaviour can kill, so it is extremely perilous.

clue.text: Not at home, going round US city no matter what

indicators.note: the away word goes round and encloses the city letters

parts.note: away means not at home
NY is New York

explanation.surface: A traveller away from home tours an American city regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyway means regardless, whatever happens.

clue.text: Sudden blow absorbed by the German dealer in cloth

indicators.note: the blow is taken inside the German article

parts.note: der is a German word for the
a rap is a sharp knock

explanation.surface: A German textile trader takes a sudden knock.
explanation.definitionFit: A draper is a shopkeeper selling fabrics, an old trade name.

clue.text: French chemist in history linked to half of Europe

parts.note: the past is history

indicators.note: the first three of the six letters are taken

explanation.surface: A French scientist in history is tied to half a continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French scientist who pioneered pasteurisation and vaccines.

clue.text: One ruling against what demonstrators carry?

definitions.meaning: a ... is, whimsically, one who bans
protesters carry a ..., a large sign on poles

explanation.surface: A judge forbids the placards carried by protesters.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner is a cloth sign; read cryptically, someone who prohibits.

clue.text: Dog associated with Hans Christian Andersen?

definitions.meaning: the fairy-tale writer was a great man from Denmark

explanation.surface: A dog is linked with the famous Danish storyteller.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals the playful second reading: Andersen as an eminent Dane.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dane is a giant breed, and Andersen was a famous Danish author.

clue.text: Former legislation is precise

parts.note: ex means former
an act is a piece of legislation

explanation.surface: An old law is described as specific.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means accurate and correct in every detail.

clue.text: Notice ends of Möbius strip rarely

indicators.note: the final letters of each of the three following words are taken

explanation.surface: Someone seldom spots a Möbius strip.
explanation.walkthrough: The Möbius strip is a famous one-sided loop in maths, decoration for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To spy is to catch sight of, to see something.

clue.text: I feel bad backing youngster as intermediary

indicators.note: going backwards, so the first two pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: to ail is to feel ill
a son is a young male child

explanation.surface: Someone regrets supporting a young person as a go-between.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses IAIL to give LIAI, then SON follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a contact person who links two parties.

clue.text: Everything is left out of poor-quality housing

indicators.note: the letter for left is taken out of the housing word

parts.note: a slum is squalid housing

explanation.surface: All the residents have moved out of the slum.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is a total, the whole amount.

clue.text: Clear a number of deliveries will be required before end of Test

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A cricket captain says a few more overs are needed before the Test match ends.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and plainly visible, not hidden.

clue.text: I encountered returning couple

indicators.note: coming back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: met means encountered

explanation.surface: Someone meets a pair on the way back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the meeting word round; 'couple' as a noun means a romantic pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic pair is often called an item.

clue.text: Stage? Run out to play guitar, perhaps

parts.note: ro is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
to strum is to play a guitar or similar instrument

explanation.surface: A musician runs off to perform on stage with a guitar.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised platform, a kind of stage for a speaker.
